findings.title: website_name bypasses untrusted user-field restrictions
findings.body: The new website_name attribute is added to the public attributes, but it is not added to untrusted_attributes (lines 105-111) like website is. For a TL0 user viewed by an anonymous user, scope.restrict_user_fields? will hide website, but website_name will still be computed from object.user_profile.website and serialized, leaking the hidden website host/path. website_name should be subject to the same untrusted restriction.

findings.title: Serializer inclusion guard is missing the required question mark
findings.body: Discourse/ActiveModel serializers use include_<attribute>? methods to decide whether an attribute is serialized. include_website_name without the trailing question mark will not be used as the inclusion hook, so the intended website.present? guard is not applied. This can serialize website_name even when it should be omitted, and may include nil values when no host can be parsed. Rename it to include_website_name? or rely on untrusted_attributes.

findings.title: Hostname comparison is naive and can produce incorrect website_name values
findings.body: The same-domain logic compares raw DNS label counts and suffixes instead of registrable domains. It can treat unrelated hosts as equivalent under shared public suffixes (for example forum.github.io vs evil.github.io, or hosts under co.uk-style suffixes) and misses some true same-registrable-domain cases such as example.com vs www.example.com when the instance hostname is the apex. This causes the wrong display name to be shown.

findings.title: Untrusted attribute spec does not cover website_name
findings.body: The test that asserts untrusted attributes are omitted for a TL0 user seen anonymously lists website but not website_name. Because website_name is derived from the restricted website field, the spec should include :website_name and assert that it is absent; otherwise the privacy regression is not caught.
